Prior to this commit the service worker only treated 504 errors as "effectively offline".
This commit changes the behaviour to treat both 503 (Service Unavailable) and 504 as "offline".

Fixes #35571

comments:
Well, a 503 status code, does not mean the server is offline. Offline would return a 504 (Gateway timeout) :grin:

Typically, it is not safe for the ServiceWorker to handle all error status codes as "offline" and just serve the cached content, so it only handles 504 that way. That said, I think it is reasonable to handle 503 as "effecticely offline", so we need to add it [here][1].

##
@alexwiese, would be interested in putting a pull request together?

[1]: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/1997b86a0/packages/service-worker/worker/src/driver.ts#L698

```
git clone https://github.com/alexwiese/angular/
cd angular
yarn install
node ./scripts/build-packages-dist.js
yarn bazel test packages/service-worker/...
```

The error is  `C:/users/alex/_bazel_alex/3tbqurya/execroot/angular/bazel-out/host/bin/external/npm/@bazel/typescript/bin/tsc_wrapped.sh: No such file or directory`

OK I spun up a brand new Ubuntu VM, installed node 12.16.1, yarn 1.21.1, ran the same commands and I get a similar error:

> error trying to exec 'cc1plus': execvp: No such file or directory

OK installing g++ fixed it. Not sure if that indicates an issue with the build scripts or the instructions.
`sudo apt-get install g++`
Once I did that on the Ubuntu VM I was able to build and test.
I have confirmed the test fails without the fix, and passes with the fix.

Thanks for figuring this out, @alexwiese :+1:

BTW, you shouldn't need `node ./scripts/build-packages-dist.js`. The `test` command should be a ble to build the necessary packages.

`g++` is indeed one of the required dependencies of bazel (see [here][1]).
